military.t: IRAN Formally Offered Hormuz Reopening for US Blockade Lift + War End. Nuclear Deferred.
military.d: AP and Axios confirmed Monday: Iran formally offered to end its Hormuz chokehold in exchange for the US lifting its blockade and ending the war — while proposing nuclear talks be deferred to a later phase. Passed to Americans via Pakistan. Two regional officials confirmed to AP. PBS: "Trump seems unlikely to accept — would leave unresolved the disagreements that led the US and Israel to go to war on Feb. 28. It doesn't address the core issue Trump cited — ensuring Iran cannot build an atomic weapon. Also silent on Iran's missile program and proxy support." CNBC (ING): "Oil is trading stronger after attempts to get peace talks back on track broke down, erasing hopes for resumption of energy flows through Hormuz anytime soon." Trump said Iran is "an active, willing participant" but also that "we have to have a deal that's acceptable to me."

military.t: ARAGHCHI Met PUTIN in St Petersburg. Putin Received MOJTABA KHAMENEI Message — First Contact.
military.d: Washington Post (AP photo), CNN and NPR confirmed: Araghchi met Putin in St. Petersburg Monday. Kremlin readout: Putin said he received a message last week from Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — first confirmed communication from the new Supreme Leader since being named. "Please convey to the Supreme Leader my appreciation for his message and my best wishes for his good health and well-being," Putin told Araghchi. Putin: Iran fighting "courageously and heroically for its independence, for its sovereignty." Araghchi briefed Putin on Pakistan-mediated diplomatic process, blamed slow progress on Washington's "destructive habits." Araghchi + Oman FM "reached some agreements" on Hormuz (NPR). Russia now formally in the deal architecture as guarantor — Mojtaba communicating via Putin signals he is alive and functional.

However Trump also said Iran is "an active, willing participant" and believes they are "negotiating in good faith." Classic Trump ambiguity — threatening bombing while acknowledging engagement. NSC meeting outcome is the key unknown for Tuesday. If Trump signals bombing resumption: Brent $115-125, Nifty sharp downward reversal from 24,093.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 9:30 AM IST. Day 60. Two months of the West Asia War. Brent at $108. A formal offer that Trump will likely reject.

THE IRAN OFFER
• Iran formally offered: Hormuz reopens if US lifts blockade AND ends the war
• Nuclear talks deferred to a later phase
• Passed to Americans via Pakistan (AP/Axios Monday)
• Trump unlikely to accept — does not address nuclear program (PBS/AP)
• Silent on missiles, proxies — core US demands
• Trump: "We have to have a deal that's acceptable to me"
• But also: Iran is "an active, willing participant, negotiating in good faith"

THE PUTIN-ARAGHCHI MEETING
• Araghchi met Putin in St Petersburg Monday (AP photo confirmed)
• Putin received a message from Mojtaba Khamenei LAST WEEK
• First confirmed communication from the new Supreme Leader
• "Convey my appreciation and best wishes for his health" — Putin to Araghchi
• Mojtaba communicating via Putin = alive, functional, using Russia as channel
• Russia formally in the guarantor architecture

MONDAY MARKETS, TUESDAY CAUTION
• Monday: Sensex +639 to 77,303, Nifty +195 to 24,093
• Rallied on Iran peace proposal — deal optimism priced in
• Tuesday: GIFT Nifty at 24,048 (-72) — partial giveback expected
• Brent $108.8 at Tuesday open
• Trump bombing review = key unknown for today's session
• Nifty 24,000 = key support level to watch

THE NEW RISK: EL NIÑO ON TOP OF HORMUZ
• NOAA: 61-70% El Niño probability June-August 2026, persisting year-end
• Below-normal monsoon + Hormuz fertiliser shortage = dual kharif disruption
• Both hitting India's June-August crop window simultaneously
• RBI: impossible tradeoff between inflation and growth rate cuts
• This is the West Asia War's most underreported India-specific risk

PAKISTAN WOUND DOWN. MINES BEING CLEARED.
• Pakistan dismantled all Islamabad security arrangements (PBS)
• No second round of talks imminent
• US clearing Iranian mines — 6 months required even after deal
• 19 vessels transited Hormuz Saturday (Windward) — slight improvement

VERDICT: Two months in. Nearly 1 billion barrels of oil disrupted. Brent at $108. An Iranian offer that falls short of US demands. A Supreme Leader communicating via Putin — alive but not seen publicly. El Niño adding a second food security threat to India's horizon. Tuesday opens cautiously. The key unknown: what does Trump's NSC meeting on bombing resumption conclude?
